# Build Playbook for TC-30412 EPB-40 Electric Park Brake Actuator

## Purpose
To outline the standard work process for the final assembly and testing of the TC-30412 EPB-40 electric park brake actuator, ensuring compliance with quality and safety standards.

## Qualifications Required
- Torque-critical qualification TQ-1 for operators at stations 40 and 50.
- One fitment audit per operator per month.

## Materials and Lots
- Housing TC-31020 (machined, in-house lot).
- Motor and ECU set TC-31110 (Larkspur Electronics - traceable, lot scan mandatory).
- Gear set TC-31140.
- Spindle assembly TC-31160.
- Case screws TC-31210 M5 x 4 (Warrigal Fasteners - traceable, single use).
- Output fastener TC-31215 M8 x 1 (Warrigal Fasteners - traceable).

## Process Steps with Control Points
1. **Station 30**: 
   - Scan the run number, housing lot, and motor set lot. The station will not advance without every traceable scan (QM-07).
   
2. **Station 40**: 
   - Seat gear set and spindle.
   - Grease dose: 2.4 g plus or minus 0.2 g from the metered dispenser.

3. **Station 50**: 
   - Fit case screws using a DC tool sequence to 6 Nm plus or minus 0.5 Nm (four screws, star order).
   - Fit output fastener to 24 Nm plus or minus 2 Nm.
   - The tool records every trace curve against the unit serial. Apply the yellow witness mark.

4. **Station 60**: 
   - Conduct a full apply-release cycle on the end-of-line rig.
   - Current draw window: 1.9 to 2.6 A.
   - Actuation time: under 900 ms.
   - Perform a park-hold load test. A fail routes the unit to the quarantine chute, not the tote.

## Quality Gates
- Every part must pass the crack-detection bench (eddy current) after washing. A reject is a critical defect; tag and quarantine.
- Every busbar set must pass the hipot bench: 3 kV DC, 60 seconds, leakage under 1 mA, plus continuity across every leg. A hipot fail is a critical defect (high-voltage safety) - quarantine chute, QM-04 applies.
- Sample the lot to the part's outgoing inspection plan; any failure quarantines the whole lot (QM-04); no partial release.

## Watch-outs from History
- **Grease Dose**: One event recorded with 8 units affected.
- **Torque Retention**: Two events recorded with 5 units affected.
- **EOL Fail Current**: One event recorded with 4 units affected.
- **Torque Out of Window**: One event recorded with 2 units affected.

## Reset/Recovery
In the event of a failure:
- Quarantine the affected units and investigate the root cause.
- Review the torque settings and grease dosing procedures.
- Ensure all operators are retrained on the critical steps and checks.
- Document the recovery actions taken and update the standard work instructions as necessary.
